business_summary.text: Hinduja Global Solutions Limited is a business process management (BPM) and digital services provider, transitioning to an intelligent experience partner with AI-led solutions. The company operates across customer experience, operations, and digital transformation with a global delivery footprint.

call_points.text: FY27 growth expected to accelerate from existing client expansion and AI digital initiatives
New client revenue ramp-up takes 6-8 months, with initial work size of $150k-$300k
Margin pressure from AI investments is seen as one-time, with operating leverage expected to return
Project Ganga is not a negative cash flow play, with pricing in line with competition
Management expects steady improvements in growth and margins over time despite near-term macro uncertainties
FY26 capex focused on AI centers of excellence, package solutions and broadband expansion with conservative leverage
79 new client signings in FY26, highest ever, with improved pipeline quality and conversion rates
Disciplined cost actions delivered 200 bps margin improvement in FY26
Net treasury and cash surplus of ₹5,346 Cr provides flexibility for strategic investments without compromising returns
Media division losses remain a concern with turnaround expected from Project Ganga and CelerityX

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: IndusInd Media & Communications Limited (IMCL), subsidiary of Hinduja Global Solutions Limited ('HGSL' or 'Company'), has imported STB and paid CVD at thetime of Import. The STB in turn installed at Customer premises against activation charge on which service tax is paid to provide Cable TVservices, which is a taxable output services. The STBs are capitalized in the Books of accounts and Company had claimed Input credit of CVD paid on capital Goods i.e. STB as the same are directly used to provide output services. Department has issued SCN denying theclaim saying that the services provided by the MSO is not directly related to the end customers and hence is not eligible for CENVAT credit (Amount involved Rs.95.55 Crore). Appeal filed with CESTAT on 10.04.2019. Matter pending before the CESTAT,will be heard in due course.
tax_litigation.status: Appeal filed with CESTAT on 10.04.2019. Matter pending before the CESTAT,will be heard in due course (i.e. The status of the matter remains the same asreported in last quarter).

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Writ petition was filed before Calcutta High Court, to quash the Show Cause Notice received on 26 Sep 2024, for the FY 2015-16 to FY2018-19 (4 years), on "Jurisdiction". Subsequently, letter received from Kolkata Customs House on 27 Feb 2025 transferring the matter tocall book list in compliance with the Calcutta High Court ('HC') order dated 14 Feb 2025 wherein interim stay was granted by the HC until the disposition of the writ petition on the grounds that Customs authorities have no jurisdiction to issue the show-cause notice on the subjectmatter of SEIS scrips issued by the issuing authority (Amount involved- INR 16,34,68,797). Proceedings are transferred to the call book list of Kolkata Customs, as per HC stay order.
tax_litigation.status: Proceedings are transferred to the call book list of Kolkata Customs, as per HC stay order. (i.e. The status of the matter remains the same as reported in last quarter).

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Penalty of INR 18,66,12,144 has been levied by the Assessing Officer (AO) underSection 271(1)(c) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 for Assessment Year 2012-13 foralleged concealment of income. This penalty predominantly pertains todisallowance of set-off of unabsorbed depreciation and brought forward businesslosses, which was claimed by the Company in its return of income (original andrevised income tax returns filed on 28.09.2012 and 29.03.2014 respectively).The tax officer denied set-off of these losses citing absence of supportingdocuments to evidence the business losses and unabsorbed depreciation in theprevious years going back to 1996-97. The Company is of the opinion that thelevy of penalty is based on the incorrect fact that business losses and unasorbeddepreciation were concealed whereas the Company had disclosed the sameyear-on-year in its tax return. The Company has filed an appeal beforeCommissioner of Income-tax (Appeals) [CIT(A)] against the said penalty order.The Company strongly believes that this penalty order is not tenable before theCIT(A) itself. Appeal has been filed.
tax_litigation.status: Appeal has been filed in the matter.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: On 23rd Oct 2024, Income Tax Department has issued a Show Cause Notice (SCN) on why General Anti- Avoidance Rules should not be invoked in relation to the demerger of NDL's media business into HGS. HGS filed its response to the SCN on 5th Dec'24 detailing why GAAR should not be applicable. On 13th Jan 2025, the Principal Commissioner Income Tax (PCIT) issued a SCN stating that he has reviewed the SCN and still holds the view that GAAR should be invoked. HGSL was given time to reply to SCN and make submissions by 28th Jan' 2025. HGS filed detailed submissions on February 21, 2025 and on March 10, 2025. There was a personal hearing before the PCIT on March 10, 2025. The Secretary GAAR panel communicated vide email dated 8 July 2025 to file a rejoinder by 28 July 2025, against the PCIT's reference to the GAAR panel on 31 March 2025. HGS has sought extension of time to file the rejoinder till 11 August 2025. (Amount involved for AY 2022-23- INR 281,59,50,487 as per Form 3CEIA of PCIT filed before the GAAR panel) further adjourned to 18 Aug 2025. GAAR panel first hearing took place on 18 August 2025 wherein Income tax department made a detailed submission before the panel and HGSL provided factual information about the demerger of DMC division of NXT digital with HGSL. Second hearing was scheduled for 15 September 2025 vide hearing notice dated 28 August 2025 and a rejoinder was filed by HGSL with the GAAR panel on 11 September 2025. The third hearing before GAAR panel happened on 15 October 2025 wherein both HGSL and the Income tax department, represented their respective submissions before the panel. Subsequently, a corrigendum was filed by the Revenue department on 15 October 2025 ( dated Sept.15th, 2025), without any prior notice to the Company. In response to which HGSL sought sufficient time, from the GAAR panel, to respond with detailed annexures and supporting documents. Panel stated that they will go through both parties' submission and pass draft order for AY22-23 and AY23-24. GAAR Panel may pass draft order for AY 2022-23 and AY 2023-24. The GAAR Panel stated that they will go through both parties' submission and pass its order for AY 22-23 and AY 23-24.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Income Tax - GAAR Panel and other related IT proceedings-
tax_litigation.status: HGSL sought sufficient time, from the GAAR panel, to respond with detailed annexures and supporting documents vide its letter dated 20 October 2025. The GAAR panel passed an order on 30 October2025, characterizing the demerger of NXT Digital’s DMC business with HGS as an “impermissible avoidance arrangement” and directed the Deputy Commissioner of Income-tax (DCIT-AO) to disregard the brought forward losses of the demerged entity, i.e., NXT Digital with the income of the resulting company, i.e., HGSL. As per the communication, total tax reduction of the Company was Rs. 281.59 Crore. Further, during the course of assessment proceedings for AY 2022-23 and AY 2023-24, the Assistant Commissioner of Income-tax has issued a notice asking for certain details on compuation of capital gains on sale of healthcare business. Tax officer is seeking to recharacterise and attribute consideration actually attributed to other jurisdictions to India and has asked for justification as to why the sale consideration earned by the Company in India should not be increased by INR 1245,67,30,765 (approximate capital gains tax impact of INR 285 crores). The Company believes that the attribution sought by the tax officer is not tenable in law and is without any valid basis. The Company is in the process of filing a detailed response to the same. No order has been passed by the tax officer on GAAR related matter. The Company had challenged the above direction and filed a writ petition in the Hon’ble High Court of Judicature at Bombay. The Hon’ble Bombay High Court heard the writ petition on December 19, 2025 and has passed an interim relief order in favour of the Company stating that: (a) the petition filed by the Company is admitted; and (b) in the interim, granted a stay on implementation of the said direction of GAAR Panel providing the interim relief to the Company. The Hon’ble High Court would further hear the matter.

Tax officer has completed the reassessment proceedings for Assessment Year 2021-22 (Financial Year 2020-21) disallowing the foreign exchange loss (net) INR 34,31,95,000 to the returned income. The tax officer has raised a tax demand of INR 8,54,65,134 and interest of INR 6,94,51,696 aggregating to INR 15,49,16,830. The tax officer has cited the absence of breakup of forex as to transaction level forex losses (net) and unrealized forex losses (net) (including that of the Phillipines branch of the Company) as the reason. The Company believes that it had filed the information requested during the course of assessment proceedings. The Company has claimed the aforementioned expenses in line with applicable provisions of section 43AA of Income-tax Act, 1961 read with applicable Income Computation and Disclosure Standards. It is in process of filing an appeal before the Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeals) against this assessment order. Further, there are multiple mistakes apparent from record in the assessment order against which the Company has filed rectification application dated 15 April 2026, which once rectified, will reduce tax demand INR 8,58,61,434 and interest to INR 1,74,65,893 aggregating to INR 10,33,27,327.

No order has been passed by the tax officer on GAAR related matter. The Company had challenged the above direction and filed a writ petition in the Hon’ble High Court of Judicature at Bombay. The Hon’ble Bombay High Court heard the writ petition on December 19, 2025 and has passed an interim relief order in favour of the Company stating that: (a) the petition filed by the Company is admitted; and (b) in the interim, granted a stay on implementation of the said direction of GAAR Panel providing the interim relief to the Company. The Hon’ble High Court would further hear the matter. The matter is currently sub-judice before the Hon’ble Bombay High Court. The next date of hearing is 24th April 2026.
tax_litigation.status: The proceedings are still under way. The next date of hearing will be fixed in the month of August 2026 by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court Bench.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: IndusInd Media & Communications Limited (IMCL), subsidiary of Hinduja Global Solutions Limited ('HGSL' or 'Company'), has imported STB and paid CVD at thetime of Import. The STB in turn installed at Customer premises against activation charge on which service tax is paid to provide Cable TVservices, which is a taxable output services. The STBs are capitalized in the Books of accounts and Company had claimed Input credit of CVD paid on capital Goods i.e. STB as the same are directly used to provide output services. Department has issued SCN denying theclaim saying that the services provided by the MSO is not directly related to the end customers and hence is not eligible for CENVAT credit (Amount involved Rs.95.55 Crore). Appeal filed with CESTAT on 10.04.2019. Matter pending before the CESTAT,will be heard in due course.
tax_litigation.status: Status Quo is maintained

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Penalty of INR 18,66,12,144 has been levied by the Assessing Officer (AO) underSection 271(1)(c) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 for Assessment Year 2012-13 foralleged concealment of income. This penalty predominantly pertains todisallowance of set-off of unabsorbed depreciation and brought forward businesslosses, which was claimed by the Company in its return of income (original andrevised income tax returns filed on 28.09.2012 and 29.03.2014 respectively).The tax officer denied set-off of these losses citing absence of supportingdocuments to evidence the business losses and unabsorbed depreciation in theprevious years going back to 1996-97. The Company is of the opinion that thelevy of penalty is based on the incorrect fact that business losses and unasorbeddepreciation were concealed whereas the Company had disclosed the sameyear-on-year in its tax return. The Company has filed an appeal beforeCommissioner of Income-tax (Appeals) [CIT(A)] against the said penalty order.The Company strongly believes that this penalty order is not tenable before the CIT(A) itself. Appeal has been filed. Hearing notice has been issued, and the Company has submitted its responses vide letters dated 17 November 2025, 19 November 2025, and 04 June 2026.
tax_litigation.status: Status Quo is maintained

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Tax officer has completed the reassessment proceedings for Assessment Year 2021-22 (Financial Year 2020-21) disallowing the foreign exchange loss (net) INR 34,31,95,000 to the returned income. The tax officer has raised a tax demand of INR 8,54,65,134 and interest of INR 6,94,51,696 aggregating to INR 15,49,16,830. The tax officer has cited the absence of breakup of forex as to transaction level forex losses (net) and unrealized forex losses (net) (including that of the Philippines branch of the Company) as the reason. The Company believes that it had filed the information requested during the course of assessment proceedings. The Company has claimed the aforementioned expenses in line with applicable provisions of section 43AA of Income-tax Act, 1961 read with applicable Income Computation and Disclosure Standards. It is in process of filing an appeal before the Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeals) against this assessment order. Further, there are multiple mistakes apparent from record in the assessment order against which the Company has filed rectification application dated 15 April 2026, which once rectified, will reduce tax demand INR 8,58,61,434 and interest to INR 1,74,65,893 aggregating to INR 10,33,27,327.
tax_litigation.status: Status quo is maintained.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Writ petition was filed before Calcutta High Court, to quash the Show Cause Notice received on 26 Sep 2024, for the FY 2015-16 to FY2018-19 (4 years), on "Jurisdiction". Subsequently, letter received from Kolkata Customs House on 27 Feb 2025 transferring the matter to call book list in compliance with the Calcutta High Court ('HC') order dated 14 Feb 2025 wherein interim stay was granted by the HC until the disposition of the writ petition on the grounds that Customs authorities have no jurisdiction to issue the show-cause notice on the subject matter of SEIS scrips issued by the issuing authority (Amount involved- INR 16,34,68,797). Proceedings are transferred to the call book list of Kolkata Customs, as per HC stay order. On March 25, 2025, Development Commissioner SEZ, Cochin, issued a SCN, based on the Company’s contention that the scrip issuing authorities did not question the excess value of duty scrips availed for ₹ 7.18 crores for two financial years of 2015-16 and 2016-17. Further, SCN issued by the Development Commissioner SEZ, Cochin is also stayed by the Hon’ble High Court of Kerala. The proceedings on merits of the writ petition will be based on the outcome of writ petition filed before the Hon’ble Calcutta High Court.
tax_litigation.status: Status Quo is maintained

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: On 23rd Oct 2024, Income Tax Department has issued a Show Cause Notice (SCN) on why General Anti- Avoidance Rules should not be invoked in relation to the demerger of NDL's media business into HGS. HGS filed its response to the SCN on 5th Dec'24 detailing why GAAR should not be applicable. On 13th Jan 2025, the Principal Commissioner Income Tax (PCIT) issued a SCN stating that he has reviewed the SCN and still holds the view that GAAR should be invoked. HGS was given time to reply to SCN and make submissions by 28th Jan' 2025. HGS filed detailed submissions on February 21, 2025 and on March 10, 2025. There was a personal hearing before the PCIT on March 10, 2025. The Secretary GAAR panel communicated vide email dated 8 July 2025 to file a rejoinder by 28 July 2025, against the PCIT's reference to the GAAR panel on 31 March 2025. HGS has sought extension of time to file the rejoinder till 11 August 2025. (Amount involved for AY 2022-23- INR 281,59,50,487 as per Form 3CEIA of PCIT filed before the GAAR panel) further adjourned to 18 Aug 2025. GAAR panel first hearing took place on 18 August 2025 wherein Income tax department made a detailed submission before the panel and HGS provided factual information about the demerger of DMC division of NXT digital with HGS. Second hearing was scheduled for 15 September 2025 vide hearing notice dated 28 August 2025 and a rejoinder was filed by HGSL with the GAAR panel on 11 September 2025. The third hearing before GAAR panel happened on 15 October 2025 wherein both HGSL and the Income tax department, represented their respective submissions before the panel. Subsequently, a corrigendum was filed by the Revenue department on 15 October 2025 ( dated Sept.15th, 2025), without any prior notice to the Company. In response to which HGSL sought sufficient time, from the GAAR panel, to respond with detailed annexures and supporting documents. Panel stated that they will go through both parties' submission and pass draft order for AY22-23 and AY23-24. GAAR Panel may pass draft order for AY 2022-23 and AY 2023-24. The GAAR Panel stated that they will go through both parties' submission and pass its order for AY 22-23 and AY 23-24. HGSL sought sufficient time, from the GAAR panel, to respond with detailed annexures and supporting documents vide its letter dated 20 October 2025. The GAAR panel passed an order on 30 October2025, characterizing the demerger of NXT Digital's DMC business with HGS as an "impermissible avoidance arrangement" and directed the Deputy Commissioner of Income-tax (DCIT-AO) to disregard the brought forward losses of the demerged entity, i.e., NXT Digital with the income of the resulting company, i.e., HGSL. As per the communication, total tax reduction of the Company was Rs. 281.59 Crore. Further, during the course of assessment proceedings for AY 2022-23 and AY 2023-24, the Assistant Commissioner of Income-tax has issued a notice asking for certain details on compuation of capital gains on sale of healthcare business. Tax officer is seeking to recharacterise and attribute consideration actually attributed to other jurisdictions to India and has asked for justification as to why the sale consideration earned by the Company in India should not be increased by INR 1245,67,30,765 (approximate capital gains tax impact of INR 285 crores). The Company believes that the attribution sought by the tax officer is not tenable in law and is without any valid basis. The Company is in the process of filing a detailed response to the same. No order has been passed by the tax officer on GAAR related matter. The Company had challenged the above direction and filed a writ petition in the Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Bombay. The Hon'ble Bombay High Court heard the writ petition on December 19, 2025 and has passed an interim relief order in favour of the Company stating that: (a) the petition filed by the Company is admitted; and (b) in the interim, granted a stay on implementation of the said direction of GAAR Panel providing the interim relief to the Company. There were multiple hearings before the Hon’ble High Court on the GAAR matter. The Hon'ble Bombay High Court is yet to fix the next hearing for this matter and status quo is maintained since the last hearing on 12 June 2026.
tax_litigation.status: Status quo is maintained since last quarter.

The Philippine BIR sent the Notice of Discrepancy ('NOD') to Hinduja Global Solutions Limited- Philippes branch for FY 2021-22 seeking various documents as part of BIR audit. Preliminary Assessment Notice ('PAN') was sent on 3 June 2025 before the receipt of Final Assessment Notice ('FAN') on 15 oct 2025, response to which was filed on 26 Nov 2025. As per FAN, BIR had computed an additional tax liability of ₱180.73M including interest and surcharge. Concerns raised by BIR are as follows: 1. Disallowed Loss made on asset retirement; 2. Overclaimed repairs and maintenance, depreciation, amortisation, electricity, and water expenses; 3. Miscellaneous income reclassified as income subject to RCIT; 4. Short deduction of EWT, WTC, and FWT; 5. Disallowed purchases per SLP validation; 6. Disallowed creditable withholding tax; 7. Unreported proceeds from divestment of healthcare business; Unreported sale of equipment; transfer of property and intangible assets deemed as sales; undeclared sales and disallowed input taxes; 8. Taxes not withheld on payment to non-resident related parties of HGS Phillipines and other third parties; 9. Deficiency in withholding taxes on purchase of goods; 10. Discrepancy between filed BIR form 1601C and Alphalist and AFS; 11. Failure to pay fringe benefit taxes on expenses incurred by the employees other than rank-and-file 12. Unpaid DST on rent and lease transactions; treasury bill transaction; on related party transaction; on short term investments held with bank; 13. Donors tax not paid on donation exceeding threshold; and 14. No approval for CAS usage; failure to submit books of accounts; Non Submission of BIR Form 2307; Non filing of BIR form 1800 Post various document submission and clarifications provided by the company to BIR, it passed the Final Decision on Disputed Assessment ('FDDA") for FY 2021–22 on 3 Sep 2026, resulting in a total assessed exposure of ₱93.14 million, comprising ₱57.51 million as basic taxes, ₱5.33 million as surcharges, and ₱30.29 million as interest computed through 30 September 2026. While several assessments were reduced or withdrawn following submission of supporting records, material liabilities remain in relation to withholding taxes, documentary stamp tax, income tax, VAT, fringe benefit tax, donor’s tax and statutory record-keeping deficiencies. Post multiple discussions and clarifications held with BIR officials and representations made by the Company before the BIR, Company agreed to settle the tax demand by paying the ₱75.37 million and taking the matter related to DST (P17M including inetrest) before the Court of Tax Appeals ('CTA').

tax_litigation.status: The Principal Commissioner at Nagpur has passed an Order-in-Original ("OIO") dated 30 January 2024 against IndusInd Media & Communications Limited (IMCL), subsidiary of Hinduja Global Solutions Limited ('HGSL' or 'Company'), in relation to the Service Tax proceedings for FY 2016-17. Based on information obtained from third-party sources, including Income-tax records (Form 26AS/TDS data), the Department has alleged that while the Company's Income-tax records reflect gross service income of approximately Rs. 510 crores during FY 2016-17, no corresponding taxable value was disclosed in the Form ST-3 returns of FY 2016-17. On this basis, the Department has treated the entire differential amount of approximately Rs. 510 crores as unreported taxable turnover and has alleged non-payment of Service Tax, proposing a Service Tax demand of approximately Rs. 76.50 crores, along with applicable interest and equivalent penalty of Rs. 76.50 crores. The adjudication proceedings culminated in the passing of the OIO ex parte. Writ Petition No. 12820 of 2026 has been filed before the Hon'ble Bombay High Court (IndusInd Media and Communication Ltd. & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.). Bombay High Court vide order dated 5 October 2026 directed that no coercive steps be taken against the Company based on the OIO until the next hearing date which is set as 8 December 2026.
